summary: The city's breakfast: puffed kachoris fried in ghee, served on leaf plates with a thin spiced potato curry and a jalebi to finish. Eaten standing, early, before the lanes fill.
Coils of fermented batter fried crisp and dropped into saffron syrup, eaten hot with the kachori or with a cup of hot milk. Thinner and crunchier in Banaras than almost anywhere else.

where: Any corner of the old city
summary: Betel leaf folded around lime, catechu, gulkand and spices, sweet or plain. Granted a Geographical Indication tag in 2023. Offered after meals, at weddings, and to anyone who lingers at a shop long enough.

season: Winter only, roughly November to February
summary: Milk churned into a saffron foam and set overnight in the winter dew, then served in a clay kulhad with pistachio. It dissolves before it can be chewed, and it exists only while the nights stay cold.

season: All year; the drink of Maha Shivratri and Holi
summary: Cold milk ground with almonds, fennel, rose, pepper and cardamom, poured over ice. On Shivratri and Holi some shops add bhang, which is legal from licensed counters in the city; ask, and start small.
Thick curd whipped with sugar and topped with a slab of malai, in a kulhad you smash afterwards. Mango, saffron and rabri versions exist, but the plain one is the test of a shop.
Tomatoes cooked down with potato, spices and ghee into a hot, sweet-sour mash, finished with crisp namak-para and coriander. Banaras's own chaat, unknown almost anywhere else.
A pastry parcel of khoya and dry fruit, sealed with a single clove, fried and dipped in syrup. Eaten warm; the clove is the signature and the name.
